title: Change and compare
goal: I can use bar models for before and after. I ask what stays the same: the total, the difference or one amount.

learn.intro: Draw a model for the Before and a model for the After. Ask first: what stays the same?

example.problem: Kumar has 60 cards. Wei has 30 cards. Kumar gives some cards to Wei. Then Kumar has 2/3 as many cards as Wei. How many cards does Kumar give?
steps: Kumar gives cards to Wei, so the total stays the same: 60 + 30 = 90.
After: Kumar has 2 units and Wei has 3 units. That is 5 units in all.
5 units = 90, so 1 unit = 18. Kumar now has 2 × 18 = 36.

howto.title: How to
steps: Draw the Before bars. Draw the After bars.
Ask what stays the same. Make that part match.
Find 1 unit. Then answer the question.

facts.title: What stays the same?
lines: A gives to B: the total.
Both get or lose the same: the difference.
Only one thing changes: the other amount.

try.text: Jason has 70 stickers. Amelia has 50 stickers. Jason gives some stickers to Amelia. Then Jason has 3/5 as many stickers as Amelia. How many stickers does Jason give? {b}
try.explanation: The total stays the same: 70 + 50 = 120. After, Jason has 3 units and Amelia has 5 units. 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15. Jason now has 3 × 15 = 45. Jason gives 70 - 45 = 25 stickers.

items.text: Nina has $96. A hat takes 3/8 of her money. A scarf takes 2/5 of the money then left.
Lily has 22 counters. Ravi has 14 counters. Lily gives 5 counters to Ravi.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The total is {b} before and after.

items.explanation: (a) 22 - 5 = 17. (b) 14 + 5 = 19. (c) 22 + 14 = 36, and 17 + 19 = 36. Giving does not change the total.

items.text: Dev is 9 years old. His uncle is 38 years old.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In 8 years Dev will be {b} and his uncle will be {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Now the uncle is {b} years older than Dev. In 8 years he is {b} years older.

items.explanation: (a) 17 and 46. (b) 29 and 29: equal years added keep the difference.

items.text: One shelf has 52 books. Another shelf has 34 books. Some books are moved from the first shelf to the second. Then both shelves have the same number of books. How many books are moved? {b}
items.explanation: The total stays 52 + 34 = 86. Each shelf has 43. The first shelf loses 52 - 43 = 9 books.

items.text: A jar holds 72 sweets. 5/12 of them are mints. How many more sweets are not mints than mints? {b}
A box has 12 red cubes and 8 blue cubes. Then 10 more red cubes are put in.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The cubes that did not change are   {circ:red|blue}

parts.label: b
parts.text: At first, blue cubes are {b} of the cubes.  (simplest form)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Now, blue cubes are {b} of the cubes.  (simplest form)

items.explanation: (a) Only red cubes were added. (b) 8 of 20 = 2/5. (c) 8 of 30 = 4/15.

items.text: Ray spent 2/5 of his money on a bag. He has $45 left. Cut the bar to show each step.

figure.alt: bar for the money, not yet cut

items.explanation: The bag takes 2 of the 5 parts. The other 3 parts are $45, so 1 part = 45 ÷ 3 = 15. All 5 parts = 5 × 15 = 75.

items.text: A pen costs 1/3 as much as a book. The pen and the book cost $28 together.
items.explanation: The book is 3 units and the pen is 1 unit. 4 units = 28, so 1 unit = 7. The pen costs 7. The book costs 3 × 7 = 21.

items.text: Mei has 3/4 as many stickers as Siti. They have 56 stickers altogether.
items.explanation: Siti has 4 units and Mei has 3 units. 7 units = 56, so 1 unit = 8. Siti has 4 × 8 = 32. Mei has 3 × 8 = 24.

items.text: What stays the same? Circle one choice for each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ali gives some marbles to Ben.   {circ:the total|the difference}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ravi and Ali are each given $5.   {circ:the total|the difference}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Red beads are added to a jar of red and blue beads.   {circ:the red beads|the blue beads}

items.explanation: (a) Ben gains what Ali loses: the total. (b) Both gain $5: the difference. (c) Only red beads go in: the blue beads.

items.text: Dev has $56. Mei has $29. Their uncle gives each child $12.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Dev has $ {b} more than Mei now.

items.explanation: (a) 56 + 12 = 68. (b) 29 + 12 = 41. (c) 68 - 41 = 27. Before the gift 56 - 29 = 27 too. The difference did not change.

items.text: Hana buys a shirt with 1/5 of her money. Shoes take 3/8 of the rest. She keeps $40. How much money did Hana start with? $ {b}
items.explanation: Shirt 2 units, shoes 3 units, left 5 units of 10 = $40. 1 unit = $8, so $80.

items.text: A jug was 5/6 full of juice. After 250 ml was poured out, it was 1/2 full. How much juice does the jug hold when it is full? {b} ml
items.explanation: 5/6 - 1/2 = 5/6 - 3/6 = 2/6 = 1/3 of the jug was poured out. 1/3 is 250 ml, so a full jug is 3 × 250 = 750 ml.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: When Ali gives Ben some stickers, the total number of stickers changes.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: When 2 children are each given $5, the difference between their money stays the same.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: If Mei has 1/2 as many cards as Ali, then Ali has 2 times as many cards as Mei.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) False: what Ali loses Ben gains. (b) True: both amounts go up by 5. (c) True: if Mei has 1 unit, Ali has 2 units.

items.text: On Monday Ravi spends 3/8 of his money. On Tuesday he spends 2/5 of what is left. After Tuesday he has $60. How much money did Ravi start with? $ {b}
items.hint: Find what fraction of all the money is left at the end.
items.explanation: Monday leaves 5/8. Tuesday takes 2/5 of 5/8 = 2/8. Left 3/8 = $60, so 1/8 = $20 and the whole is $160.

items.text: Ali and Ben have 132 cards altogether. Ben gives 14 cards to Ali. Then Ben has 4/7 as many cards as Ali. How many cards did Ben have at first? {b}
items.hint: The total stays the same. Find each child's cards after.
items.explanation: After: Ben 4 units, Ali 7 units. 11 units = 132, so 1 unit = 12. Ben has 48 now. Before giving 14 he had 48 + 14 = 62.

items.text: Ravi is 42 years old. His son is 12 years old. In how many years will the son be 1/3 of his father's age? {b} years
items.hint: The difference in their ages never changes. How many units is it?
items.explanation: The difference stays 30 years. The son is 1 unit and the father 3 units, so 2 units = 30. 1 unit = 15, which is 3 years from now.

items.text: Ali, Ben and Cara have 150 stickers altogether. Ali has twice as many stickers as Ben. Ben has 10 more than Cara.
items.hint: Call Cara's stickers 1 unit. Draw bars for Ben and for Ali.
items.explanation: Cara 1 unit, Ben 1 unit + 10, Ali 2 units + 20. 4 units + 30 = 150, so 1 unit = 30. Cara 30, Ben 40, Ali 80.

items.text: In a hall, 2/5 of the people are children. Then 15 adults leave and 15 children come in. Now 1/2 of the people are children. How many people are in the hall? {b}
items.hint: The total stays the same. How much more of the total is children?
items.explanation: The total is the same. 1/2 - 2/5 = 1/10 of the total is 15, so the total is 150.

items.text: A jar holds red beads and white beads. Red beads make up 2/7 of the jar. Then 24 red beads are taken out. Now red beads make up 1/6 of the jar. How many beads were in the jar at first? {b}
items.hint: The white beads do not change. What fraction of each total is white?
items.explanation: The white beads stay the same: 5/7 of the start and 5/6 of the end. White is 5 parts, so the total goes from 7 parts to 6 parts. 1 part = 24, so 7 × 24 = 168.

items.text: Ali and Ben have 120 marbles altogether. Ali gives 1/3 of his marbles to Ben. Then Ben has 3 times as many marbles as Ali. How many marbles did Ali have at first? {b}
items.hint: After giving, Ali has 2/3 of his marbles. Ben has 3 times that.
items.explanation: Ali has 3 units and keeps 2. Ben then has 6 units. 2 + 6 = 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15 and Ali had 45.

items.text: Jenny pays 1/5 of her money for a book. A bag takes 1/2 of the rest. She keeps $24. How much money did Jenny start with? $ {b}
items.explanation: Book 1 unit, bag 2 units, left 2 units = $24. 1 unit = $12, so $60.

items.text: Jamie has 46 cards. Jason has 30 cards. Jamie gives some cards to Jason. Then they have equal numbers. How many cards does Jamie give? {b}
items.explanation: The total is 76, so each has 38. Jamie has 46 - 38 = 8 too many. Jamie gives 8 cards.

items.text: Amelia has $50. Ray has $30. They are each given the same amount. Then Ray has 3/4 as much as Amelia. How much is each given? $ {b}
items.explanation: The difference stays $20 = 1 unit. Amelia now has $80, so the gift is $30.

items.text: A pond has 24 ducks and 16 geese. Then 24 more geese come to the pond.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The birds that did not change are   {circ:ducks|geese}

parts.label: b
parts.text: The fraction of birds that are ducks is now {b}

items.explanation: (a) Only geese came, so the 24 ducks did not change. (b) Now there are 24 + 40 = 64 birds. 24/64 = 3/8.
